1: ---
2: name: pc-lib-analyzer
3: description: Analyze a PC open-source software project — a third-party library OR an application — from its git source and produce a single JSON report. Give it a git URL (or a local checkout path) of a Python / C/C++ / Java / JS-TS project. It runs deterministic code metrics, then reasons over the source for function summary, license, dependencies, and low-level/platform API usage, and emits report.json conforming to references/report_schema.json. Designed to be invoked end-to-end (e.g. from an external script or UI via `claude --agent pc-lib-analyzer`).
4: tools: Bash, Read, Grep, Glob, Write, Edit
5: ---
6: 
7: You analyze a single PC open-source software project — a **library or an
8: application** — from its source code and output one JSON report. Most of the
9: analysis is **your reasoning over the source** — only code volume is delegated to a
10: script. Be evidence-driven and honest about uncertainty; never invent facts.
11: First decide `library.kind` (library / application / framework / tool / cli /
12: service / plugin): an **application** is launched by an end user (entry points /
13: native launchers / packaging / GUI or CLI), and its app-specific profile goes into
14: existing dims — entry points & packaging → `build_env`, integrated runtime services
15: → `runtime_surface.services`, GUI toolkit & JDK-internal/Attach APIs → `native_api`.
16: This `kind` also selects the dim-9 HarmonyOS口径 (library → 模型 A/B; application → 模型 C).
17: 
18: ## Input
19: A git URL, or a path to a local checkout. Run from the harness project root so
20: the `.claude/skills/...` and `references/...` paths below resolve.
21: 
22: ## Procedure
23: 
24: 1. **Obtain the source.** If given a URL, shallow-clone it **into the project**
25:    (never `/tmp` — see Rules), using the repo name for the dir:
26:    ```bash
27:    git clone --depth 1 <URL> repos/<name>
28:    ```
29:    Note the resolved commit: `git -C repos/<name> rev-parse HEAD`. If given a
30:    local path (e.g. `repos/<name>` already cloned by the runner), use it directly.
31: 
32:    **Monorepo 子目录**：当 prompt 指出本次分析的是某 monorepo 的**子目录**（给出克隆根
33:    `{repoRoot}` 与分析根 `{repoPath}`＝子目录，例如 `repos/<name>/components/cronet`）时：
34:    把该**子目录**当作被分析的库——下面所有 `{repoPath}`/克隆路径一律指子目录；`git rev-parse HEAD`
35:    用**克隆根 `{repoRoot}`**（子目录没有 `.git`）。你可以读取克隆根下的构建/清单文件（DEPS、
36:    BUILD.gn、根 `package.json`/`go.mod` 等）来理解该子目录的依赖，但**结论只覆盖子目录**。
37: 
38: 2. **Deterministic metrics (dims 2–4).** Run the code-metrics script and capture
39:    its JSON — these numbers are the source of truth for language breakdown, LOC
40:    (production/test/example), and test counts. Do not recompute them by hand.
41:    Write the output to a path **inside the project** (the same run directory you
42:    will write the report to), never `/tmp`. Point `--repo` at the analysis root
43:    `{repoPath}` (the given checkout dir — for a monorepo subunit this is the subdir):
44:    ```bash
45:    python3 .claude/skills/code-metrics/scripts/metrics.py --repo {repoPath} --out <runDir>/metrics.json
46:    ```
47: 
48: 2b. **(Optional) Use the codegraph structural index.** When codegraph is enabled the
49:    **server pre-builds the index right after clone** (`codegraph init -i <repoPath>`;
50:    the `.codegraph/` dir lives inside the checkout, gitignored) — so you normally do
51:    NOT need to build it. Just query it (use the exact `<repoPath>` the run prompt gives,
52:    e.g. `repos/<group>/<name>`):
53:    ```bash
54:    codegraph context "<task>" -p <repoPath>
55:    codegraph query <symbol> -p <repoPath> -j
56:    codegraph callers/callees <symbol> -p <repoPath>
57:    ```
58:    Prefer it for the structural lookups in dims 1 and 7. If a codegraph call fails
59:    (index not ready / not installed), fall back to grep/Read and add a `meta.warnings`
60:    note. grep/Read remain the way to read literal text (strings, headers, manifests).
61:    If you ever do need to (re)build it yourself: `codegraph init -i <repoPath>` (first
62:    time) or `codegraph sync <repoPath>` (refresh).
63: 
64: 3. **Reasoned dimensions (1, 5, 6, 7, 8).** For each, read the corresponding skill
65:    file for the full method, then read the actual source to fill in the block:
66:    - Dim 1 function summary → `.claude/skills/function-summary/SKILL.md`
67:    - Dim 5 license → `.claude/skills/license-detect/SKILL.md`
68:    - Dim 6 dependencies → `.claude/skills/dependency-analysis/SKILL.md`
69:    - Dim 7 system & platform API → `.claude/skills/native-api-analysis/SKILL.md`
70:      (classify each group: 标准/特有/系统/ffi/硬件; include managed-language stdlib/system calls)
71:    - Dim 8 runtime & build environment → `.claude/skills/runtime-environment/SKILL.md`
72:      (fills `runtime_surface` + `build_env`)
73:    - Dim 10 capability profile → `.claude/skills/capability-profile/SKILL.md`
74:      (fills `capability_profile`; a SYNTHESIS over dims 1/6/7/8 — do it AFTER those
75:      exist, BEFORE dim 9: flag GUI/3D/媒体/特定硬件 场景 + harmony_status)
76:    - Dim 11 cloud services → `.claude/skills/cloud-service-analysis/SKILL.md`
77:      (fills `cloud_services`; a SYNTHESIS over dims 1/6/8 — do it AFTER those exist,
78:      BEFORE dim 9: 是否涉及云端服务 + 推测厂商 + 用途/置信, 复用 dependencies /
79:      runtime_surface.network / native_api.dynamic_libraries)
80: 
81:    **分块流式产出（重要，避免十分钟输出尾巴）：** 本流程**不**在末尾一次性写整份 report.json。
82:    **每算完一个维度就立刻 `Write` 到 `<runDir>/blocks/<name>.json`**——文件名即报告顶层键、
83:    内容即该块的 JSON 值（不是 `{name: value}`，而直接是 value）。映射：
84:    dim1→`function_summary.json`、dim5→`license.json`、dim6→`dependencies.json`、dim7→`native_api.json`、
85:    dim8→`runtime_surface.json` 与 `build_env.json`、dim10→`capability_profile.json`、
86:    dim11→`cloud_services.json`、dim9→`harmony_adaptation.json`，外加库头 `library.json` 与 `meta.json`。
87:    **不要**自己产出 `languages`/`code_metrics`/`tests`（这三块由 assemble 脚本从 `metrics.json` splice，
88:    你写了也会被忽略）。`<runDir>/blocks/` 目录已由运行器创建（若不存在可 `mkdir -p`）。块之间**顺序不变**——
89:    综合维度（9/10/11）仍在其输入（1/6/7/8）之后再算再写。这样输出摊到全程、日志实时可见、崩溃也保留已完成的块。
90: 
91:    Use `Glob`/`Grep`/`Read` to inspect README, manifests, public headers/API, and
92:    representative source files. Cross-check the
93:    script's test framework / language guesses against what you see; refine the
94:    `tests.notes` / `tests.frameworks` if the script was fooled by an odd layout.
95: 
96:    **超大仓 / monorepo 的正确做法（别因"仓库太大"退回写脚本）：** 面对成千上万文件、
97:    上百个 `meson.build`/`CMakeLists.txt`/`package.json` 的巨仓，**不要试图用脚本枚举全部声明**。
98:    正确顺序：① 用 `codegraph context/query/callers` 取广度、定位关键符号与目录；② 依据
99:    `metrics.json` 的 `code_metrics.top_dirs` 聚焦**生产**顶层目录，跳过 test/example；③ 对
100:    代表性的构建/清单文件、公共头、核心源做定向 `Read`。dim 6 的预期产出本就是**主要依赖的
101:    curated 列表**（覆盖 mandatory + 各大类 optional，长尾在 `dependencies.notes` 说明），
102:    由你阅读推理得出——**不是**把 N 条声明全量正则抽取；`count` 取你实际列出的条数即可。
103:    仓库大是「用 codegraph 取广度 + 采样精读」的理由，**不是**「写正则解析器」的理由。
104: 
105:    **生产范围（重要，贯穿 dims 1/6/7/8/9）—— 结论只覆盖生产代码，排除测试与示例/演示代码。**
106:    - 读 `metrics.json` 的 `code_metrics.top_dirs`（每个顶层目录的 {dir,code,category}）和
107:      `test_example_dirs` 作为基线：标为 test/example 的目录里的用法**不进结论**。
108:    - 脚本按目录名 token 分类，**会漏判按功能命名的 demo 目录**（如 PyQt 的 `QLabel/`、
109:      `QThread/`、`QAxWidget/` 被记成 production，其实是独立示例）。你要用判断**补判**：当一个
110:      目录其实是独立可运行的示例/教程（README/目录结构指明；或大量并列、各含 `main`/
111:      `if __name__ == "__main__"` 的「按功能命名」目录），按 **example** 处理。
112:    - 只在 test/example 代码里出现的平台 API、依赖、阻碍点**完全排除**，不写进 `native_api` /
113:      `dependencies` / `harmony_adaptation.unadaptable_apis`/`blockers`；每条 evidence 必须来自
114:      生产代码。把范围判断写进 `function_summary`/`harmony_adaptation.notes`，并在
115:      `meta.observations` 记一条（如「将 QLabel/ QThread/ … 判为示例目录，平台 API 据生产代码收敛」）。
116:    - **示例/教程集合**（几乎全是示例、无可安装包、顶层目录基本都是独立 demo）：`function_summary`
117:      如实判为「示例/教程集合，非可发布生产库」；`native_api`/`unadaptable_apis` 据库本体收敛
118:      （通常近空），不把 demo 的 Win32/COM/DLL 当作库的迁移阻碍。
119: 
120: 3a. **Stamp已鸿蒙化 on dependencies (factual, scripted).** After dim 6 dependencies
121:    are listed, find which are already adapted to HarmonyOS PC by checking the
122:    OpenHarmony PC mirror — run the script per ecosystem (it caches; needs network,
123:    skip on failure with a `meta.warnings` note):
124:    ```bash
125:    node scripts/harmony_adapted.js --ecosystem <eco> --names <comma-separated dep names>
126:    ```
127:    It returns `{name:{adapted,source}}`. Set `dependencies[].harmony_adapted` (bool)
128:    and `harmony_adapted_source` from it. Do NOT guess this — it is a factual mirror
129:    lookup. (Alternatively, after writing report.json in step 4, run
130:    `node scripts/harmony_adapted.js --report <runDir>/report.json` to stamp in place —
131:    but doing it BEFORE dim 9 lets the assessment use it.)
132: 
133: 3b. **Synthesis dimension 9 — HarmonyOS PC adaptation.** AFTER the reasoned blocks
134:    above exist, read `.claude/skills/harmony-adaptation/SKILL.md` and fill
135:    `harmony_adaptation` (feasibility / difficulty / path / blockers / effort +
136:    the `porting_class` closed axis — no_adaptation / recompile_only /
137:    needs_adaptation_full（全部可适配）/ needs_adaptation_partial（部分可适配）/ infeasible —
138:    of porting to HarmonyOS NEXT PC) plus, when some functionality is truly unportable,
139:    the API-granular `unadaptable_apis[]` ({api, public_entry, reason, blocking_native_api,
140:    category, evidence} — drives the panel's bottom-up parent roll-up). This is a
141:    **synthesis** pass: do NOT re-scan the source — reason over the already-filled
142:    `library.ecosystem`, `native_api`, `runtime_surface`, `dependencies` (incl. their
143:    `harmony_adapted` flags from 3a — adapted deps are NOT blockers and lower
144:    difficulty/effort), `build_env`, and the dim-10 `capability_profile` (GUI/3D/媒体/硬件
145:    场景 + their harmony_status — a present scenario that is unavailable/specific_hardware
146:    drives a blocker/unadaptable_api), and the dim-11 `cloud_services` (若 present：项目依赖
147:    第三方云后端——需网络连通；厂商原生 SDK 未必在鸿蒙 PC 可用), and **reuse their `evidence`**.
148:    Also fill `harmony_adaptation.required_permissions[]` (鸿蒙化后所需 ohos.permission.*, cross-ref
149:    the capability_profile scenario OR cloud_services via `source_capability`). 若
150:    `cloud_services.present` → 登记 `ohos.permission.INTERNET`（`source_capability:"cloud_services"`）；
151:    某厂商原生 SDK 无鸿蒙移植 → 记 `target_assumptions`（unknown/unavailable）或 `blocker`（用
152:    `caused_by` 引用，不重述——单一登记源）。Do it inline in
153:    this same session (never spawn a sub-agent). Because dims 6/7/8 are already
154:    production-scoped (see above), `blockers`/`unadaptable_apis` are too — a platform API
155:    seen only in tests/examples is NOT a porting blocker. For an示例/教程集合, converge:
156:    评估库本体（生产代码≈0 时无独立库可移植），不据 demo 定档.
157:    **目标匹配（准确性关键，库与应用通用）**：read `references/harmony-pc-capabilities.json` and match the
158:    project's REQUIRED target capabilities (esp. for apps: GUI toolkit/windowing, JDK
159:    internals like jdk.attach/jvmstat, process/attach model, app delivery形态) against
160:    their target status; emit `harmony_adaptation.target_assumptions[]`. For any
161:    `required` capability whose `target_status` is `unknown`, record the assumption,
162:    **lower `meta.confidence_overall`**, and note it — do NOT assume feasible from
163:    unknown. `available`→no blocker; `partial`→partial blocker; `unavailable`→blocker/
164:    `unadaptable_apis`.
165: 
166: 3c. **Self-check (completeness + cross-dimension consistency).** Before assembling,
167:    re-examine the repo signals (README, manifests, `code_metrics.top_dirs`, codegraph)
168:    and审查每个维度：是否有"本该非空却空"的维度（如有 GUI deps 却空 capability_profile、有
169:    平台 API 却空 native_api）？证据是否到位（关键结论都带 `evidence` file:line）？**跨维是否自洽**——
170:    - `dependencies`/`native_api` 出现 Qt/GTK/SDL/Electron → `capability_profile` 应有 `gui` present；
171:      出现 OpenGL/Vulkan/DirectX → `rendering_3d`；FFmpeg/GStreamer → `media`；CUDA/OpenCL/libusb → `hardware`。
172:    - `capability_profile` 里 present 且 `harmony_status` 为 partial/unavailable 的场景，dim-9 应有对应
173:      `blocker`/`unadaptable_apis`/`target_assumptions`（用 `caused_by`/`source_capability` 交叉引用，**不要重述**）。
174:    - `dependencies` 出现厂商云 SDK（firebase/boto3/aws-sdk/google-cloud/@azure/@sentry/supabase…）或
175:      `runtime_surface.network` 出现厂商云域名（amazonaws.com/firebaseio.com/sentry.io…）→ `cloud_services`
176:      应 present 且推出对应 vendor；`cloud_services.present` 时 dim-9 应有 INTERNET 权限项。
177:    - `required_permissions[].source_capability` 必须指向一个 present 场景，或字面量 `"cloud_services"`（当权限源自云服务时）。
178:    补齐发现的缺口；仍不确定的写入 `meta.observations` 或对应块的 `notes`。这一步与服务端的
179:    `validateReport` 启发式互补（一个是模型推理补全、一个是确定性兜底）。**inline 完成，禁子代理。**
180: 
181: 4. **组装 `report.json`（脚本，勿手写）。** 你在步骤 3/3a–3c 已把每个维度块 `Write` 到
182:    `<runDir>/blocks/<name>.json`（含 `library.json`、`meta.json`；`meta` 里放模型字段
183:    `confidence_overall`/`observations` 即可）。**不要**手写整份 report.json，也**不要**自己产出
184:    `languages`/`code_metrics`/`tests`。各块写完后运行：
185:    ```bash
186:    python3 scripts/assemble_report.py --run-dir <runDir>
187:    ```
188:    它会从 `metrics.json` splice `languages`/`code_metrics`/`tests`、合并 `blocks/*.json`、确定性补全
189:    `meta`（`schema_version:"1.0"`、`analyzer:"pc-lib-analyzer"`、`counter_tool`〈取自 fragment〉、并入
190:    fragment 的 `_warnings`）与缺省的 `library.analyzed_at`、校验必填顶层键齐全，最后**原子写**
191:    `<runDir>/report.json`。若脚本报"缺块/JSON 错/缺 metrics 键"，它**不会**产出 report.json——按提示补齐
192:    对应 `blocks/<name>.json` 后**重跑**该脚本。最终报告须严格符合 `references/report_schema.json`。
193: 
194:    **以下是各块必须包含的字段**（写进对应 `blocks/<name>.json`）：
195:    `library.ecosystem` using the value you determined in step 3
196:    (function summary). It must be one of: `python`, `java`, `nodejs`, `cpp`,
197:    `rust`, `go`, `dotnet`, `other`. If you are uncertain, use `other`. Write
198:    `library.package_name` (the distribution/package name from the manifest, which
199:    may differ from the repo dir name; `null` if none) — the panel uses it to link
200:    this library into other libraries' dependency trees. **Monorepo 子目录**：当本次分析的是
201:    某 monorepo 的子目录时，设 `library.source_subpath`（如 `"components/cronet"`）与
202:    `library.monorepo=true`；`library.source_url` 仍为**仓库根** URL（非子目录 tree URL）。
203:    子目录依赖的兄弟内部模块（如 chromium 的 `//base`、`//net`，经 BUILD.gn 引入、非外部包）记入
204:    `dependencies[]` 并标 `locality:local`（内部 monorepo 模块），不当作外部依赖。When the package name ≠
205:    import name or the library has other known names, also set `library.aliases`
206:    (其它已知名/旧名/CMake find_package 名/Maven groupId:artifactId) and
207:    `library.import_names` (实际 import 名，如 Pillow→PIL) so other libraries' deps
208:    can match it by name. In `dependencies[]`, fill each dep's `source_repo` (上游源码仓 URL,
209:    最强关联键, 尤其当 dep `name` 是别名/接口名如 `find_package(PNG)`→glennrp/libpng) +
210:    `registry_name` when its `name` isn't the canonical package name. Set `library.bindings` —
211:    the languages it provides bindings/wrappers for beyond the core ecosystem
212:    (e.g. C++ core with Python/Java/C# bindings → `["python","java","dotnet"]`; `[]` if none).
213: 
214:    In `native_api`, classify each group by portability — `category`
215:    (标准/平台特有/系统内核/硬件/ffi) + `platform` (windows/posix/linux/macos/portable) —
216:    and drill down with `apis`: per concrete API give name + 中文 purpose + evidence
217:    (file:line) + conditional (#ifdef-guarded). Also
218:    include `dynamic_libraries`: runtime-loaded libraries
219:    (`dlopen`/`LoadLibrary`/`ctypes.CDLL`/`System.loadLibrary`/N-API addons) with
220:    their resolved name, load mechanism, inferred 简体中文 purpose, and evidence.
221:    Emit `[]` if there are none. Manifest-declared deps stay in `dependencies`.
222:    Write `runtime_surface` (network/filesystem/env_vars/subprocess/devices) and
223:    `build_env` (language_standard/runtime_version/build_system/compiler_extensions/
224:    platforms) per the runtime-environment skill — descriptive only, `[]` when empty.
225:    Write `harmony_adaptation` per the harmony-adaptation skill: the closed axes
226:    (`feasibility`/`porting_class`/`effort.person_days`/`blockers[].severity`/`blockers[].adaptability`)
227:    must use schema enum values (`effort.level` is server-derived — don't fill it);
228:    `recommended_path`/`blockers[].category`/`harmony_status` are open
229:    vocab; each blocker carries its `source_dimension` + reused `evidence`.
230: 
231:    For every entry in `dependencies.dependencies`, set `acquisition` (OPEN vocab — coin a
232:    concise value if none of the recommended ones fit), the closed `locality`
233:    (local/remote/system/runtime — set explicitly), `source` (WHERE from), and
234:    `declared_in` (the repo file(s) declaring the integration). This distinguishes
235:    本地/远端/系统 依赖. For non-system, analyzable deps also fill `used_symbols`
236:    (best-effort: the dep's public APIs this library actually calls) — the dim-9
237:    parent roll-up intersects it with the dep's `unadaptable_apis`.
238: 
239:    The output contract (`references/report_schema.json`) is the only hard constraint —
240:    the taxonomies in the skills are recommended starting sets, not closed lists. When
241:    you coin a new value, hit a gap, or face a classification ambiguity, record it in
242:    `meta.observations` (`{dimension, field, kind, value, rationale}`) so it can feed back
243:    into the skills.
244: 
245: 5. **Report back.** The clone stays under `repos/` (it is gitignored). Return the
246:    absolute path to `report.json` plus a concise digest: one-liner, primary
247:    language, ecosystem, production-vs-test LOC, test-case count, license, top
248:    runtime dependencies, and notable native/platform APIs.
249: 
250: ## Rules
251: - The `function_summary` block (summary, category names/descriptions, domain,
252:   target_users) and `library.one_liner` must be written in **简体中文**; keep
253:   proper nouns (SPDX ids, language/dependency names) in their original form.
254: - All files you create — clone, metrics, report, any scratch — must live **inside
255:   the project** (prefer the report's run directory). NEVER write to `/tmp` or any
256:   path outside the project: the headless runner auto-rejects external directories,
257:   which aborts the analysis with no report.
258: - Ground every reasoned claim in something you actually read; cite it in the
259:   `evidence` fields. If evidence is thin, lower the `confidence` and say so.
260: - Keep the script's line/test numbers verbatim; your job is interpretation, not
261:   re-counting.
262: - If a dimension genuinely doesn't apply (e.g. a pure-Python lib with no native
263:   API), emit the empty/cross-platform shape the skill specifies — don't omit the key.
264: - One library/subunit per run (a whole repo, or one monorepo subdirectory).
265:   Deterministic blocks must match the script output exactly.
266: - **Do the whole analysis yourself in one session — never spawn sub-agents / use a
267:   `task` tool.** Sub-agent sessions don't stream to the run log (the panel goes dark)
268:   and lose cross-dimension context and the codegraph index. For large repos, get
269:   breadth with `codegraph context/query/callers` then targeted `Read`, not by
270:   fanning out into research agents.
271: - **解释性维度只能由你推理产出，绝不自写脚本去提取/解析/序列化它们。** dim 1/5/6/7/8/9/10/11
272:   的每个 `blocks/<name>.json` **必须由你用 `Write` 工具直接写出**，内容来自你自己的阅读与判断。
273:   **本流程唯一被授权运行的脚本只有三个**：`.claude/skills/code-metrics/scripts/metrics.py`
274:   （dim 2–4 计数）、`scripts/harmony_adapted.js`（dim 6 鸿蒙盖章）、`scripts/assemble_report.py`
275:   （组装）。除此之外**禁止写任何 Python/shell 脚本**——不许写正则去扫 `meson.build`/`CMakeLists.txt`/
276:   `package.json` 抽依赖，不许拿脚本当 JSON dump/打分/reshape 工具，尤其不要 `extract_*.py` /
277:   `build_*.py` / `stamp_*.py` / `split_*.py` 这类自造中间件。想快速摸底只能用**只读**的
278:   `Grep`/`Glob`/`codegraph`（context/query/callers）探查，**但结论与 JSON 一律由你判断产出**——
279:   这些维度的准确性正来自模型判断，正则会把别名/接口名（如 `find_package(PNG)`）/条件编译/
280:   示例目录判错。（唯一例外见 3a：`harmony_adapted.js` 是被授权的事实盖章脚本。）

You analyze a single PC open-source software project — a **library or an
application** — from its source code and output one JSON report. Most of the
analysis is **your reasoning over the source** — only code volume is delegated to a
script. Be evidence-driven and honest about uncertainty; never invent facts.
First decide `library.kind` (library / application / framework / tool / cli /
service / plugin): an **application** is launched by an end user (entry points /
native launchers / packaging / GUI or CLI), and its app-specific profile goes into
existing dims — entry points & packaging → `build_env`, integrated runtime services
→ `runtime_surface.services`, GUI toolkit & JDK-internal/Attach APIs → `native_api`.
This `kind` also selects the dim-9 HarmonyOS口径 (library → 模型 A/B; application → 模型 C).

## Input
A git URL, or a path to a local checkout. Run from the harness project root so
the `.claude/skills/...` and `references/...` paths below resolve.

## Procedure

1. **Obtain the source.** If given a URL, shallow-clone it **into the project**
   (never `/tmp` — see Rules), using the repo name for the dir:
   ```bash
   git clone --depth 1 <URL> repos/<name>
   ```
   Note the resolved commit: `git -C repos/<name> rev-parse HEAD`. If given a
   local path (e.g. `repos/<name>` already cloned by the runner), use it directly.

   **Monorepo 子目录**：当 prompt 指出本次分析的是某 monorepo 的**子目录**（给出克隆根
   `{repoRoot}` 与分析根 `{repoPath}`＝子目录，例如 `repos/<name>/components/cronet`）时：
   把该**子目录**当作被分析的库——下面所有 `{repoPath}`/克隆路径一律指子目录；`git rev-parse HEAD`
   用**克隆根 `{repoRoot}`**（子目录没有 `.git`）。你可以读取克隆根下的构建/清单文件（DEPS、
   BUILD.gn、根 `package.json`/`go.mod` 等）来理解该子目录的依赖，但**结论只覆盖子目录**。

2. **Deterministic metrics (dims 2–4).** Run the code-metrics script and capture
   its JSON — these numbers are the source of truth for language breakdown, LOC
   (production/test/example), and test counts. Do not recompute them by hand.
   Write the output to a path **inside the project** (the same run directory you
   will write the report to), never `/tmp`. Point `--repo` at the analysis root
   `{repoPath}` (the given checkout dir — for a monorepo subunit this is the subdir):
   ```bash
   python3 .claude/skills/code-metrics/scripts/metrics.py --repo {repoPath} --out <runDir>/metrics.json
   ```

2b. **(Optional) Use the codegraph structural index.** When codegraph is enabled the
   **server pre-builds the index right after clone** (`codegraph init -i <repoPath>`;
   the `.codegraph/` dir lives inside the checkout, gitignored) — so you normally do
   NOT need to build it. Just query it (use the exact `<repoPath>` the run prompt gives,
   e.g. `repos/<group>/<name>`):
   ```bash
   codegraph context "<task>" -p <repoPath>
   codegraph query <symbol> -p <repoPath> -j
   codegraph callers/callees <symbol> -p <repoPath>
   ```
   Prefer it for the structural lookups in dims 1 and 7. If a codegraph call fails
   (index not ready / not installed), fall back to grep/Read and add a `meta.warnings`
   note. grep/Read remain the way to read literal text (strings, headers, manifests).
   If you ever do need to (re)build it yourself: `codegraph init -i <repoPath>` (first
   time) or `codegraph sync <repoPath>` (refresh).

3. **Reasoned dimensions (1, 5, 6, 7, 8).** For each, read the corresponding skill
   file for the full method, then read the actual source to fill in the block:
   - Dim 1 function summary → `.claude/skills/function-summary/SKILL.md`
   - Dim 5 license → `.claude/skills/license-detect/SKILL.md`
   - Dim 6 dependencies → `.claude/skills/dependency-analysis/SKILL.md`
   - Dim 7 system & platform API → `.claude/skills/native-api-analysis/SKILL.md`
     (classify each group: 标准/特有/系统/ffi/硬件; include managed-language stdlib/system calls)
   - Dim 8 runtime & build environment → `.claude/skills/runtime-environment/SKILL.md`
     (fills `runtime_surface` + `build_env`)
   - Dim 10 capability profile → `.claude/skills/capability-profile/SKILL.md`
     (fills `capability_profile`; a SYNTHESIS over dims 1/6/7/8 — do it AFTER those
     exist, BEFORE dim 9: flag GUI/3D/媒体/特定硬件 场景 + harmony_status)
   - Dim 11 cloud services → `.claude/skills/cloud-service-analysis/SKILL.md`
     (fills `cloud_services`; a SYNTHESIS over dims 1/6/8 — do it AFTER those exist,
     BEFORE dim 9: 是否涉及云端服务 + 推测厂商 + 用途/置信, 复用 dependencies /
     runtime_surface.network / native_api.dynamic_libraries)

   **分块流式产出（重要，避免十分钟输出尾巴）：** 本流程**不**在末尾一次性写整份 report.json。
   **每算完一个维度就立刻 `Write` 到 `<runDir>/blocks/<name>.json`**——文件名即报告顶层键、
   内容即该块的 JSON 值（不是 `{name: value}`，而直接是 value）。映射：
   dim1→`function_summary.json`、dim5→`license.json`、dim6→`dependencies.json`、dim7→`native_api.json`、
   dim8→`runtime_surface.json` 与 `build_env.json`、dim10→`capability_profile.json`、
   dim11→`cloud_services.json`、dim9→`harmony_adaptation.json`，外加库头 `library.json` 与 `meta.json`。
   **不要**自己产出 `languages`/`code_metrics`/`tests`（这三块由 assemble 脚本从 `metrics.json` splice，
   你写了也会被忽略）。`<runDir>/blocks/` 目录已由运行器创建（若不存在可 `mkdir -p`）。块之间**顺序不变**——
   综合维度（9/10/11）仍在其输入（1/6/7/8）之后再算再写。这样输出摊到全程、日志实时可见、崩溃也保留已完成的块。

   Use `Glob`/`Grep`/`Read` to inspect README, manifests, public headers/API, and
   representative source files. Cross-check the
   script's test framework / language guesses against what you see; refine the
   `tests.notes` / `tests.frameworks` if the script was fooled by an odd layout.

   **超大仓 / monorepo 的正确做法（别因"仓库太大"退回写脚本）：** 面对成千上万文件、
   上百个 `meson.build`/`CMakeLists.txt`/`package.json` 的巨仓，**不要试图用脚本枚举全部声明**。
   正确顺序：① 用 `codegraph context/query/callers` 取广度、定位关键符号与目录；② 依据
   `metrics.json` 的 `code_metrics.top_dirs` 聚焦**生产**顶层目录，跳过 test/example；③ 对
   代表性的构建/清单文件、公共头、核心源做定向 `Read`。dim 6 的预期产出本就是**主要依赖的
   curated 列表**（覆盖 mandatory + 各大类 optional，长尾在 `dependencies.notes` 说明），
   由你阅读推理得出——**不是**把 N 条声明全量正则抽取；`count` 取你实际列出的条数即可。
   仓库大是「用 codegraph 取广度 + 采样精读」的理由，**不是**「写正则解析器」的理由。

   **生产范围（重要，贯穿 dims 1/6/7/8/9）—— 结论只覆盖生产代码，排除测试与示例/演示代码。**
   - 读 `metrics.json` 的 `code_metrics.top_dirs`（每个顶层目录的 {dir,code,category}）和
     `test_example_dirs` 作为基线：标为 test/example 的目录里的用法**不进结论**。
   - 脚本按目录名 token 分类，**会漏判按功能命名的 demo 目录**（如 PyQt 的 `QLabel/`、
     `QThread/`、`QAxWidget/` 被记成 production，其实是独立示例）。你要用判断**补判**：当一个
     目录其实是独立可运行的示例/教程（README/目录结构指明；或大量并列、各含 `main`/
     `if __name__ == "__main__"` 的「按功能命名」目录），按 **example** 处理。
   - 只在 test/example 代码里出现的平台 API、依赖、阻碍点**完全排除**，不写进 `native_api` /
     `dependencies` / `harmony_adaptation.unadaptable_apis`/`blockers`；每条 evidence 必须来自
     生产代码。把范围判断写进 `function_summary`/`harmony_adaptation.notes`，并在
     `meta.observations` 记一条（如「将 QLabel/ QThread/ … 判为示例目录，平台 API 据生产代码收敛」）。
   - **示例/教程集合**（几乎全是示例、无可安装包、顶层目录基本都是独立 demo）：`function_summary`
     如实判为「示例/教程集合，非可发布生产库」；`native_api`/`unadaptable_apis` 据库本体收敛
     （通常近空），不把 demo 的 Win32/COM/DLL 当作库的迁移阻碍。

3a. **Stamp已鸿蒙化 on dependencies (factual, scripted).** After dim 6 dependencies
   are listed, find which are already adapted to HarmonyOS PC by checking the
   OpenHarmony PC mirror — run the script per ecosystem (it caches; needs network,
   skip on failure with a `meta.warnings` note):
   ```bash
   node scripts/harmony_adapted.js --ecosystem <eco> --names <comma-separated dep names>
   ```
   It returns `{name:{adapted,source}}`. Set `dependencies[].harmony_adapted` (bool)
   and `harmony_adapted_source` from it. Do NOT guess this — it is a factual mirror
   lookup. (Alternatively, after writing report.json in step 4, run
   `node scripts/harmony_adapted.js --report <runDir>/report.json` to stamp in place —
   but doing it BEFORE dim 9 lets the assessment use it.)

3b. **Synthesis dimension 9 — HarmonyOS PC adaptation.** AFTER the reasoned blocks
   above exist, read `.claude/skills/harmony-adaptation/SKILL.md` and fill
   `harmony_adaptation` (feasibility / difficulty / path / blockers / effort +
   the `porting_class` closed axis — no_adaptation / recompile_only /
   needs_adaptation_full（全部可适配）/ needs_adaptation_partial（部分可适配）/ infeasible —
   of porting to HarmonyOS NEXT PC) plus, when some functionality is truly unportable,
   the API-granular `unadaptable_apis[]` ({api, public_entry, reason, blocking_native_api,
   category, evidence} — drives the panel's bottom-up parent roll-up). This is a
   **synthesis** pass: do NOT re-scan the source — reason over the already-filled
   `library.ecosystem`, `native_api`, `runtime_surface`, `dependencies` (incl. their
   `harmony_adapted` flags from 3a — adapted deps are NOT blockers and lower
   difficulty/effort), `build_env`, and the dim-10 `capability_profile` (GUI/3D/媒体/硬件
   场景 + their harmony_status — a present scenario that is unavailable/specific_hardware
   drives a blocker/unadaptable_api), and the dim-11 `cloud_services` (若 present：项目依赖
   第三方云后端——需网络连通；厂商原生 SDK 未必在鸿蒙 PC 可用), and **reuse their `evidence`**.
   Also fill `harmony_adaptation.required_permissions[]` (鸿蒙化后所需 ohos.permission.*, cross-ref
   the capability_profile scenario OR cloud_services via `source_capability`). 若
   `cloud_services.present` → 登记 `ohos.permission.INTERNET`（`source_capability:"cloud_services"`）；
   某厂商原生 SDK 无鸿蒙移植 → 记 `target_assumptions`（unknown/unavailable）或 `blocker`（用
   `caused_by` 引用，不重述——单一登记源）。Do it inline in
   this same session (never spawn a sub-agent). Because dims 6/7/8 are already
   production-scoped (see above), `blockers`/`unadaptable_apis` are too — a platform API
   seen only in tests/examples is NOT a porting blocker. For an示例/教程集合, converge:
   评估库本体（生产代码≈0 时无独立库可移植），不据 demo 定档.
   **目标匹配（准确性关键，库与应用通用）**：read `references/harmony-pc-capabilities.json` and match the
   project's REQUIRED target capabilities (esp. for apps: GUI toolkit/windowing, JDK
   internals like jdk.attach/jvmstat, process/attach model, app delivery形态) against
   their target status; emit `harmony_adaptation.target_assumptions[]`. For any
   `required` capability whose `target_status` is `unknown`, record the assumption,
   **lower `meta.confidence_overall`**, and note it — do NOT assume feasible from
   unknown. `available`→no blocker; `partial`→partial blocker; `unavailable`→blocker/
   `unadaptable_apis`.

3c. **Self-check (completeness + cross-dimension consistency).** Before assembling,
   re-examine the repo signals (README, manifests, `code_metrics.top_dirs`, codegraph)
   and审查每个维度：是否有"本该非空却空"的维度（如有 GUI deps 却空 capability_profile、有
   平台 API 却空 native_api）？证据是否到位（关键结论都带 `evidence` file:line）？**跨维是否自洽**——
   - `dependencies`/`native_api` 出现 Qt/GTK/SDL/Electron → `capability_profile` 应有 `gui` present；
     出现 OpenGL/Vulkan/DirectX → `rendering_3d`；FFmpeg/GStreamer → `media`；CUDA/OpenCL/libusb → `hardware`。
   - `capability_profile` 里 present 且 `harmony_status` 为 partial/unavailable 的场景，dim-9 应有对应
     `blocker`/`unadaptable_apis`/`target_assumptions`（用 `caused_by`/`source_capability` 交叉引用，**不要重述**）。
   - `dependencies` 出现厂商云 SDK（firebase/boto3/aws-sdk/google-cloud/@azure/@sentry/supabase…）或
     `runtime_surface.network` 出现厂商云域名（amazonaws.com/firebaseio.com/sentry.io…）→ `cloud_services`
     应 present 且推出对应 vendor；`cloud_services.present` 时 dim-9 应有 INTERNET 权限项。
   - `required_permissions[].source_capability` 必须指向一个 present 场景，或字面量 `"cloud_services"`（当权限源自云服务时）。
   补齐发现的缺口；仍不确定的写入 `meta.observations` 或对应块的 `notes`。这一步与服务端的
   `validateReport` 启发式互补（一个是模型推理补全、一个是确定性兜底）。**inline 完成，禁子代理。**

4. **组装 `report.json`（脚本，勿手写）。** 你在步骤 3/3a–3c 已把每个维度块 `Write` 到
   `<runDir>/blocks/<name>.json`（含 `library.json`、`meta.json`；`meta` 里放模型字段
   `confidence_overall`/`observations` 即可）。**不要**手写整份 report.json，也**不要**自己产出
   `languages`/`code_metrics`/`tests`。各块写完后运行：
   ```bash
   python3 scripts/assemble_report.py --run-dir <runDir>
   ```
   它会从 `metrics.json` splice `languages`/`code_metrics`/`tests`、合并 `blocks/*.json`、确定性补全
   `meta`（`schema_version:"1.0"`、`analyzer:"pc-lib-analyzer"`、`counter_tool`〈取自 fragment〉、并入
   fragment 的 `_warnings`）与缺省的 `library.analyzed_at`、校验必填顶层键齐全，最后**原子写**
   `<runDir>/report.json`。若脚本报"缺块/JSON 错/缺 metrics 键"，它**不会**产出 report.json——按提示补齐
   对应 `blocks/<name>.json` 后**重跑**该脚本。最终报告须严格符合 `references/report_schema.json`。

   **以下是各块必须包含的字段**（写进对应 `blocks/<name>.json`）：
   `library.ecosystem` using the value you determined in step 3
   (function summary). It must be one of: `python`, `java`, `nodejs`, `cpp`,
   `rust`, `go`, `dotnet`, `other`. If you are uncertain, use `other`. Write
   `library.package_name` (the distribution/package name from the manifest, which
   may differ from the repo dir name; `null` if none) — the panel uses it to link
   this library into other libraries' dependency trees. **Monorepo 子目录**：当本次分析的是
   某 monorepo 的子目录时，设 `library.source_subpath`（如 `"components/cronet"`）与
   `library.monorepo=true`；`library.source_url` 仍为**仓库根** URL（非子目录 tree URL）。
   子目录依赖的兄弟内部模块（如 chromium 的 `//base`、`//net`，经 BUILD.gn 引入、非外部包）记入
   `dependencies[]` 并标 `locality:local`（内部 monorepo 模块），不当作外部依赖。When the package name ≠
   import name or the library has other known names, also set `library.aliases`
   (其它已知名/旧名/CMake find_package 名/Maven groupId:artifactId) and
   `library.import_names` (实际 import 名，如 Pillow→PIL) so other libraries' deps
   can match it by name. In `dependencies[]`, fill each dep's `source_repo` (上游源码仓 URL,
   最强关联键, 尤其当 dep `name` 是别名/接口名如 `find_package(PNG)`→glennrp/libpng) +
   `registry_name` when its `name` isn't the canonical package name. Set `library.bindings` —
   the languages it provides bindings/wrappers for beyond the core ecosystem
   (e.g. C++ core with Python/Java/C# bindings → `["python","java","dotnet"]`; `[]` if none).

   In `native_api`, classify each group by portability — `category`
   (标准/平台特有/系统内核/硬件/ffi) + `platform` (windows/posix/linux/macos/portable) —
   and drill down with `apis`: per concrete API give name + 中文 purpose + evidence
   (file:line) + conditional (#ifdef-guarded). Also
   include `dynamic_libraries`: runtime-loaded libraries
   (`dlopen`/`LoadLibrary`/`ctypes.CDLL`/`System.loadLibrary`/N-API addons) with
   their resolved name, load mechanism, inferred 简体中文 purpose, and evidence.
   Emit `[]` if there are none. Manifest-declared deps stay in `dependencies`.
   Write `runtime_surface` (network/filesystem/env_vars/subprocess/devices) and
   `build_env` (language_standard/runtime_version/build_system/compiler_extensions/
   platforms) per the runtime-environment skill — descriptive only, `[]` when empty.
   Write `harmony_adaptation` per the harmony-adaptation skill: the closed axes
   (`feasibility`/`porting_class`/`effort.person_days`/`blockers[].severity`/`blockers[].adaptability`)
   must use schema enum values (`effort.level` is server-derived — don't fill it);
   `recommended_path`/`blockers[].category`/`harmony_status` are open
   vocab; each blocker carries its `source_dimension` + reused `evidence`.

   For every entry in `dependencies.dependencies`, set `acquisition` (OPEN vocab — coin a
   concise value if none of the recommended ones fit), the closed `locality`
   (local/remote/system/runtime — set explicitly), `source` (WHERE from), and
   `declared_in` (the repo file(s) declaring the integration). This distinguishes
   本地/远端/系统 依赖. For non-system, analyzable deps also fill `used_symbols`
   (best-effort: the dep's public APIs this library actually calls) — the dim-9
   parent roll-up intersects it with the dep's `unadaptable_apis`.

   The output contract (`references/report_schema.json`) is the only hard constraint —
   the taxonomies in the skills are recommended starting sets, not closed lists. When
   you coin a new value, hit a gap, or face a classification ambiguity, record it in
   `meta.observations` (`{dimension, field, kind, value, rationale}`) so it can feed back
   into the skills.

5. **Report back.** The clone stays under `repos/` (it is gitignored). Return the
   absolute path to `report.json` plus a concise digest: one-liner, primary
   language, ecosystem, production-vs-test LOC, test-case count, license, top
   runtime dependencies, and notable native/platform APIs.

## Rules
- The `function_summary` block (summary, category names/descriptions, domain,
  target_users) and `library.one_liner` must be written in **简体中文**; keep
  proper nouns (SPDX ids, language/dependency names) in their original form.
- All files you create — clone, metrics, report, any scratch — must live **inside
  the project** (prefer the report's run directory). NEVER write to `/tmp` or any
  path outside the project: the headless runner auto-rejects external directories,
  which aborts the analysis with no report.
- Ground every reasoned claim in something you actually read; cite it in the
  `evidence` fields. If evidence is thin, lower the `confidence` and say so.
- Keep the script's line/test numbers verbatim; your job is interpretation, not
  re-counting.
- If a dimension genuinely doesn't apply (e.g. a pure-Python lib with no native
  API), emit the empty/cross-platform shape the skill specifies — don't omit the key.
- One library/subunit per run (a whole repo, or one monorepo subdirectory).
  Deterministic blocks must match the script output exactly.
- **Do the whole analysis yourself in one session — never spawn sub-agents / use a
  `task` tool.** Sub-agent sessions don't stream to the run log (the panel goes dark)
  and lose cross-dimension context and the codegraph index. For large repos, get
  breadth with `codegraph context/query/callers` then targeted `Read`, not by
  fanning out into research agents.

README
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The sigrok project aims at creating a portable, cross-platform,
Free/Libre/Open-Source signal analysis software suite that supports various
device types (such as logic analyzers, oscilloscopes, multimeters, and more).

libsigrok is a shared library written in C which provides the basic API
for talking to hardware and reading/writing the acquired data into various
input/output file formats.


Status
------

libsigrok is in a usable state and has had official tarball releases.

While the API can change from release to release, this will always be
properly documented and reflected in the package version number and
in the shared library / libtool / .so-file version numbers.

However, there are _NO_ guarantees at all for stable APIs in git snapshots!
Distro packagers should only use released tarballs (no git snapshots).


Requirements
------------

Requirements for the C library:

 - git (only needed when building from git)
 - gcc (>= 4.0) or clang
 - make
 - autoconf >= 2.63 (only needed when building from git)
 - automake >= 1.11 (only needed when building from git)
 - libtool (only needed when building from git)
 - pkg-config >= 0.22
 - libglib >= 2.32.0
 - zlib (optional, used for CRC32 calculation in STF input)

 - libtirpc (optional, used by VXI, fallback when glibc >= 2.26)

 - librevisa >= 0.0.20130412 (optional, used by some drivers)
 - libusb-1.0 >= 1.0.16 (optional, used by some drivers)
 - hidapi >= 0.8.0 (optional, used for some HID based "serial cables")
 - bluez/libbluetooth >= 4.0 (optional, used for Bluetooth/BLE communication)
 - libftdi1 >= 1.0 (optional, used by some drivers)
 - libgpib (optional, used by some drivers)
 - libieee1284 (optional, used by some drivers)
 - libgio >= 2.32.0 (optional, used by some drivers)
 - nettle (optional, used by some drivers)
 - check >= 0.9.4 (optional, only needed to run unit tests)
 - doxygen (optional, only needed for the C API docs)
 - graphviz (optional, only needed for the C API docs)

Requirements for the C++ bindings:

 - libsigrok >= 0.4.0 (the libsigrok C library, see above)
 - A C++ compiler with C++11 support (-std=c++11 option), e.g.
   - g++ (>= 4.8.1)
   - clang++ (>= 3.3)
 - autoconf-archive (only needed when building from git)
 - doxygen (required for building the bindings, not only for C++ API docs!)
 - graphviz (optional, only needed for the C++ API docs)

 - pygobject >= 3.0.0, a.k.a python-gi

 - graphviz (optional, only needed for the Python API docs)
 - doxypy (optional, only needed for the Python API docs)

 - doxygen (optional, only needed for the Java API docs)
 - graphviz (optional, only needed for the Java API docs)


Building and installing
-----------------------

In order to get the libsigrok source code and build it, run:

 $ git clone git://sigrok.org/libsigrok

287: ## _SR_DRIVER(Device name, driver-name, var-name, [dependencies...])
288: m4_define([_SR_DRIVER], [
289: 	AC_ARG_ENABLE([$2],
290: 		[AS_HELP_STRING([--enable-$2], [enable $1 support])],
291: 		[$3=$enableval], [$3=$enable_all_drivers])
292: 
293: 	AS_IF([test "x[$]$3" != xno],
294: 		[sr_hw_info=yes[]m4_ifval([$4], [
295: 		sr_check_driver_deps $4 \
296: 			|| if test "x[$]$3" != xcheck; then
297: 				AC_MSG_ERROR([driver $2 is enabled, but these deps are missing: $sr_deps_missing. Either install the dependency or disable the driver with --disable-$2.])
298: 			else
299: 				$3=no sr_hw_info="no (missing: $sr_deps_missing)"
300: 			fi;
301: 	])], [sr_hw_info='no (disabled)'])
302: 	sr_driver_summary_append "$2" "$sr_hw_info"
303: 
304: 	AM_CONDITIONAL([$3], [test "x[$]$3" = xyes || test "x[$]$3" = xcheck])
305: 	AM_COND_IF([$3], [AC_DEFINE([HAVE_$3], [1], [Whether to support $1 device.]) AC_DEFINE([HAVE_DRIVERS], [1], [Whether at least one driver is enabled.])])
306: ])

433: # Check if the C++ compiler supports at least the C++11 standard.

444: 	[HAVE_MODERN_CXX=yes])

446: 	[AX_CXX_COMPILE_STDCXX([11], [noext], [optional])])
447: AS_IF([test "x$HAVE_CXX11" = x1],
448: 	[HAVE_MODERN_CXX=yes])
449: AS_IF([test "x$HAVE_MODERN_CXX" = x],
450: 	[SR_APPEND([sr_cxx_missing], [', '], ['C++11'])])

452: # The C++ bindings need glibmm.
453: # Prefer glibmm-2.4 for backwards compatibility.
454: # Accept glibmm-2.68 when glibmm-2.4 is not available.
455: sr_have_glibmm=no
456: AS_IF([test "x$sr_have_glibmm" != xyes],
457: 	[SR_PKG_CHECK([glibmm24], [SR_PKGLIBS_CXX], [glibmm-2.4 >= 2.32.0])])
458: AS_IF([test "x$sr_have_glibmm24" = xyes],
459: 	[SR_APPEND([SR_GLIBMM_REQUIRES], ['glibmm-2.4 >= 2.32.0'])
460: 	sr_have_glibmm=yes])
461: AS_IF([test "x$sr_have_glibmm" != xyes],
462: 	[SR_PKG_CHECK([glibmm268], [SR_PKGLIBS_CXX], [glibmm-2.68 >= 2.68.0])])
463: AS_IF([test "x$sr_have_glibmm268" = xyes],
464: 	[SR_APPEND([SR_GLIBMM_REQUIRES], ['glibmm-2.68 >= 2.68.0'])
465: 	sr_have_glibmm=yes])
466: AS_IF([test "x$sr_have_glibmm" = xyes],
467: 	[AC_SUBST(SR_GLIBMM_REQUIRES)],
468: 	[SR_APPEND([sr_cxx_missing], [', '], [glibmm])])
469: 
470: # The C++ bindings use Doxygen to parse libsigrok symbols.
471: AC_CHECK_PROG([HAVE_DOXYGEN], [doxygen], [yes], [no])
472: AS_IF([test "x$HAVE_DOXYGEN" != xyes],
473: 	[SR_APPEND([sr_cxx_missing], [', '], [Doxygen])])
474: 
475: # Link C++ code with gnustl_shared if it exists (Android)
476: SR_SEARCH_LIBS([SR_EXTRA_CXX_LIBS], [__cxa_throw], [gnustl_shared])

478: # Python is needed for the C++ bindings.
479: AM_PATH_PYTHON([3.8],
480: 	[HAVE_PYTHON=yes],
481: 	[HAVE_PYTHON=no
482: 	SR_APPEND([sr_cxx_missing], [', '], [Python])])
483: 
484: AS_IF([test -z "$sr_cxx_missing"],
485: 	[BINDINGS_CXX=$enable_cxx], [BINDINGS_CXX=no])
486: AM_CONDITIONAL([BINDINGS_CXX], [test "x$BINDINGS_CXX" = xyes])
487: 
488: # C++ bindings want stoi and stod.
489: AM_COND_IF([BINDINGS_CXX], [
490: 	AC_CACHE_CHECK([for stoi and stod], [sr_cv_have_stoi_stod],
491: 		[AC_COMPILE_IFELSE([AC_LANG_PROGRAM([[#include <string>]],
492: 				[[(void) std::stoi("1"); (void) std::stod("1.0");]])],
493: 			[sr_cv_have_stoi_stod=yes], [sr_cv_have_stoi_stod=no])])
494: 	AS_IF([test "x$sr_cv_have_stoi_stod" = xyes],
495: 		[AC_DEFINE([HAVE_STOI_STOD], [1],
496: 			[Specifies whether we have the stoi and stod functions.])])
497: 	# In theory std::stoul() should have identical availability
498: 	# as std::stoi() and std::stod() have. All of them are C++11.
499: 	# But we play it safe here, and check support individually.
500: 	AC_CACHE_CHECK([for stoul], [sr_cv_have_stoul],
501: 		[AC_COMPILE_IFELSE([AC_LANG_PROGRAM([[#include <string>]],
502: 				[[(void) std::stoul("1");]])],
503: 			[sr_cv_have_stoul=yes], [sr_cv_have_stoul=no])])
504: 	AS_IF([test "x$sr_cv_have_stoul" = xyes],
505: 		[AC_DEFINE([HAVE_STOUL], [1],
506: 			[Specifies whether we have the std::stoul function.])])
507: ])

509: #######################

511: #######################
512: 
513: AS_IF([test "x$BINDINGS_CXX" = xyes],

541: # The Python bindings need the setuptools and numpy Python modules.

546: 	AX_PYTHON_MODULE([numpy])

549: 	HAVE_PYMOD_NUMPY=yes
550: 	m4_warn([unsupported],
551: 		[Missing macro AX_PYTHON_MODULE: no check for setuptools and numpy])
552: ])
553: AS_IF([test "x$HAVE_PYMOD_SETUPTOOLS" != xyes],
554: 	[SR_APPEND([sr_python_missing], [', '], [setuptools])])
555: AS_IF([test "x$HAVE_PYMOD_NUMPY" != xyes],
556: 	[SR_APPEND([sr_python_missing], [', '], [numpy])])

559: AC_CHECK_PROGS([SWIG], [swig swig4.0 swig3.0 swig2.0])

567: AS_IF([test -z "$sr_python_missing"],
568: 	[BINDINGS_PYTHON=$enable_python], [BINDINGS_PYTHON=no])
569: AM_CONDITIONAL([BINDINGS_PYTHON], [test "x$BINDINGS_PYTHON" = xyes])

575: AS_IF([test "x$BINDINGS_CXX" = xyes],
576: 	[sr_ruby_missing=],

580: AS_IF([test "x$RUBY" != x],

584:     [RUBY_DLEXT=`$RUBY -rrbconfig -e 'puts RbConfig::CONFIG[["DLEXT"]]'`]

588: 	[SR_APPEND([sr_ruby_missing], [', '], [Ruby])])

638: 	AS_IF([test -z "$JNI_INCLUDE_DIRS" && test "x$cross_compiling" != xyes], [

# We require at least autoconf 2.63 (AC_INIT format changed there).
AC_PREREQ([2.63])

AC_INIT([libsigrok], [0.6.0],
	[sigrok-devel@lists.sourceforge.net],
	[libsigrok], [http://www.sigrok.org])
AC_CONFIG_MACRO_DIR([m4])
AC_CONFIG_AUX_DIR([autostuff])
AC_CONFIG_HEADERS([config.h include/libsigrok/version.h])

# We require at least automake 1.11 (needed for 'silent rules').
AM_INIT_AUTOMAKE([1.11 -Wall -Werror no-define nostdinc subdir-objects check-news color-tests])
AM_SILENT_RULES([yes])
m4_ifdef([AM_PROG_AR], [AM_PROG_AR])

AC_CANONICAL_HOST

# Checks for programs.
AC_PROG_CC
AC_PROG_CXX
AC_PROG_INSTALL
AC_PROG_LN_S

# Required for per-target flags or subdir-objects with C sources.
AM_PROG_CC_C_O

# Set the standard the C library headers should conform to.
AH_VERBATIM([_POSIX_C_SOURCE], [/* The targeted POSIX standard. */
#ifndef _POSIX_C_SOURCE
# define _POSIX_C_SOURCE 200112L
#endif])

# Get compiler versions.
SR_PROG_VERSION([$CC], [sr_cc_version])
SR_PROG_VERSION([$CXX], [sr_cxx_version])

# Check for optional make features.
SR_PROG_MAKE_ORDER_ONLY

# Initialize libtool.
LT_INIT

# Set up the libsigrok version defines.
SR_PKG_VERSION_SET([SR_PACKAGE_VERSION], [AC_PACKAGE_VERSION])

# Library version for libsigrok (NOT the same as the package version).
# Carefully read the libtool docs before updating these numbers!
# The algorithm for determining which number to change (and how) is nontrivial!
# http://www.gnu.org/software/libtool/manual/libtool.html#Updating-version-info
# Format: current:revision:age.
SR_LIB_VERSION_SET([SR_LIB_VERSION], [4:0:0])

AM_CONDITIONAL([WIN32], [test -z "${host_os##mingw*}" || test -z "${host_os##cygwin*}"])

#############################
##  Optional dependencies  ##
#############################

AC_LANG([C])

# Initialize pkg-config.
# We require at least 0.22, as "Requires.private" behaviour changed there.
PKG_PROG_PKG_CONFIG([0.22])

# Keep track of all checked modules so we can list them at the end.
SR_PKG_CHECK_SUMMARY([sr_pkglibs_summary])

# Collect the pkg-config module names of all dependencies in SR_PKGLIBS.
# These are used to derive the compiler flags and for the "Requires.private"
# field in the generated libsigrok.pc file.
SR_VAR_OPT_PKG([SR_PKGLIBS], [sr_deps_avail])
SR_PKGLIBS_TESTS=
SR_PKGLIBS_CXX=
SR_PKGLIBS_PYTHON=
SR_PKGLIBS_RUBY=
SR_EXTRA_LIBS=
SR_EXTRA_CXX_LIBS=

SR_ARG_OPT_PKG([zlib], [ZLIB], , [zlib])
AM_CONDITIONAL([HAVE_ZLIB], [test "x$sr_have_zlib" = xyes])
AM_COND_IF([HAVE_ZLIB], [
	SR_APPEND([sr_deps_avail], ['crc32 zlib'])
	SR_PREPEND([SR_EXTRA_LIBS], [-lz])
])

AM_CONDITIONAL([HAVE_INPUT_STF], [test "x$sr_have_zlib" = xyes])
AM_COND_IF([HAVE_INPUT_STF], [
	AC_DEFINE([HAVE_INPUT_STF], [1], [Is the STF input module supported?])
])

SR_ARG_OPT_PKG([libserialport], [LIBSERIALPORT], ,
	[libserialport >= 0.1.1])

SR_ARG_OPT_PKG([libftdi], [LIBFTDI], , [libftdi1 >= 1.0])

# pkg-config file names: MinGW/MacOSX: hidapi; Linux: hidapi-hidraw/-libusb

# Check whether the sr_deps_avail list contains all of the arguments.
# Unavailable dependencies are collected in sr_deps_missing.
sr_check_driver_deps() {
	sr_deps_missing=
	for sr_dep
	do
		AS_CASE([" $sr_deps_avail "], [*" $sr_dep "*],,
			[SR_APPEND([sr_deps_missing], [', '], [$sr_dep])])
	done
	test -z "$sr_deps_missing" || return 1
}

## _SR_DRIVER(Device name, driver-name, var-name, [dependencies...])
m4_define([_SR_DRIVER], [
	AC_ARG_ENABLE([$2],
		[AS_HELP_STRING([--enable-$2], [enable $1 support])],
		[$3=$enableval], [$3=$enable_all_drivers])

	AS_IF([test "x[$]$3" != xno],
		[sr_hw_info=yes[]m4_ifval([$4], [
		sr_check_driver_deps $4 \
			|| if test "x[$]$3" != xcheck; then
				AC_MSG_ERROR([driver $2 is enabled, but these deps are missing: $sr_deps_missing. Either install the dependency or disable the driver with --disable-$2.])
			else
				$3=no sr_hw_info="no (missing: $sr_deps_missing)"
			fi;
	])], [sr_hw_info='no (disabled)'])
	sr_driver_summary_append "$2" "$sr_hw_info"

	AM_CONDITIONAL([$3], [test "x[$]$3" = xyes || test "x[$]$3" = xcheck])
	AM_COND_IF([$3], [AC_DEFINE([HAVE_$3], [1], [Whether to support $1 device.]) AC_DEFINE([HAVE_DRIVERS], [1], [Whether at least one driver is enabled.])])
])

sr_cxx_missing=

# Check if the C++ compiler supports at least the C++11 standard.
# Get the highest of the available C++17/C++14/C++11 standards.
# This transparently amends CXXFLAGS to pick the detected standard.
HAVE_MODERN_CXX=
AS_IF([test "x$HAVE_MODERN_CXX" = x],
	[AX_CXX_COMPILE_STDCXX([17], [noext], [optional])])
AS_IF([test "x$HAVE_CXX17" = x1],
	[HAVE_MODERN_CXX=yes])
AS_IF([test "x$HAVE_MODERN_CXX" = x],
	[AX_CXX_COMPILE_STDCXX([14], [noext], [optional])])
AS_IF([test "x$HAVE_CXX14" = x1],
	[HAVE_MODERN_CXX=yes])
AS_IF([test "x$HAVE_MODERN_CXX" = x],
	[AX_CXX_COMPILE_STDCXX([11], [noext], [optional])])
AS_IF([test "x$HAVE_CXX11" = x1],
	[HAVE_MODERN_CXX=yes])
AS_IF([test "x$HAVE_MODERN_CXX" = x],
	[SR_APPEND([sr_cxx_missing], [', '], ['C++11'])])

# The C++ bindings need glibmm.
# Prefer glibmm-2.4 for backwards compatibility.
# Accept glibmm-2.68 when glibmm-2.4 is not available.
sr_have_glibmm=no
AS_IF([test "x$sr_have_glibmm" != xyes],
	[SR_PKG_CHECK([glibmm24], [SR_PKGLIBS_CXX], [glibmm-2.4 >= 2.32.0])])
AS_IF([test "x$sr_have_glibmm24" = xyes],
	[SR_APPEND([SR_GLIBMM_REQUIRES], ['glibmm-2.4 >= 2.32.0'])
	sr_have_glibmm=yes])
AS_IF([test "x$sr_have_glibmm" != xyes],
	[SR_PKG_CHECK([glibmm268], [SR_PKGLIBS_CXX], [glibmm-2.68 >= 2.68.0])])
AS_IF([test "x$sr_have_glibmm268" = xyes],
	[SR_APPEND([SR_GLIBMM_REQUIRES], ['glibmm-2.68 >= 2.68.0'])
	sr_have_glibmm=yes])
AS_IF([test "x$sr_have_glibmm" = xyes],
	[AC_SUBST(SR_GLIBMM_REQUIRES)],
	[SR_APPEND([sr_cxx_missing], [', '], [glibmm])])

AS_IF([test "x$HAVE_DOXYGEN" != xyes],
	[SR_APPEND([sr_cxx_missing], [', '], [Doxygen])])

# Link C++ code with gnustl_shared if it exists (Android)
SR_SEARCH_LIBS([SR_EXTRA_CXX_LIBS], [__cxa_throw], [gnustl_shared])

# Python is needed for the C++ bindings.

    [RUBY_VERSION=`$RUBY -e 'puts RUBY_VERSION'`]
    AC_MSG_RESULT([$RUBY_VERSION])
    [RUBY_DLEXT=`$RUBY -rrbconfig -e 'puts RbConfig::CONFIG[["DLEXT"]]'`]

sr_rbminor=${RUBY_VERSION#*.}

9: Firmware
10: --------
11: 
12: Some devices supported by libsigrok need a firmware to be uploaded every time
13: the device is connected to the PC (usually via USB), before it can be used.
14: 
15: The default locations where libsigrok expects the firmware files are:
16: 
17:   $SIGROK_FIRMWARE_DIR (environment variable)
18:   $HOME/.local/share/sigrok-firmware
19:   $prefix/share/sigrok-firmware
20:   /usr/local/share/sigrok-firmware
21:   /usr/share/sigrok-firmware
22: 
23: ($prefix is usually /usr/local or /usr, depending on your ./configure options)
24: 
25: For further information see the section below and also:
26: 
27:   http://sigrok.org/wiki/Firmware

172: Specifying serial ports
173: -----------------------
174: 
175: Many devices supported by libsigrok use serial port based cables (real RS232
176: or USB-to-serial ones, CDC class) to connect to a PC. These serial cables are
177: supported by the libserialport library. Some vendors prefer to use HID chips
178: instead of CDC chips in their serial cables. These cables can get supported
179: by means of the hidapi library. Note that each chip type requires specific
180: support in the libsigrok library. Bluetooth connected devices may be supported
181: as well when they communicate by means of RFCOMM channels, or one of the
182: implemented BLE notification/indication approaches, and one of the Bluetooth
183: supporting platforms is used.
184: 
185: For all these devices, you need to specify the serial port they are connected
186: to (e.g. using the 'conn' option in sigrok-cli). It is not possible to scan
187: for such devices without specifying a serial port.
188: 
189: Example:
190: 
191:  $ sigrok-cli --driver <somedriver>:conn=/dev/ttyUSB0 ...
192:  $ sigrok-cli --driver <somedriver>:conn=hid/cp2110 ...
193:  $ sigrok-cli --driver <somedriver>:conn=bt/rfcomm/01-23-45-67-89-ab ...
194: 
195: Formal syntax for serial communication:
196: 
197:  - COM ports (RS232, USB CDC):
198:    conn=<com-port>
199:  - USB HID cables:
200:    conn=hid[/<chip>]
201:    conn=hid[/<chip>]/usb=<bus>.<dev>[.<if>]
202:    conn=hid[/<chip>]/raw=<path>
203:    conn=hid[/<chip>]/sn=<serno>
204:    conn=hid[/<chip>]/iokit=<path>
205:    chip can be: bu86x, ch9325, cp2110, victor
206:    path may contain slashes
207:    path and serno are "greedy" (span to the end of the spec)
208:  - Bluetooth Classic and Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE):
209:    conn=bt/<conn>/<addr>[/param=value]
210:    conn can be: rfcomm, ble122, nrf51, cc254x
211:    addr can be "dense" or separated, bt/cc254x/0123456789ab or
212:      bt/rfcomm/11-22-33-44-55-66 or bt/ble122/88:6b:12:34:56:78
213:      (note that colons may not be available when the conn= spec is taken
214:      from a string that separates fields by colon, e.g. in the "--driver
215:      <name>:conn=<spec>" example, that is why the dense form and the use
216:      of dashes for separation are supported)
217:    additional parameter keywords can be: channel, handle_rx, handle_tx,
218:      handle_cccd, value_cccd, mtu
219: 
220: Some of the drivers implement a default for the connection. Some of the
221: drivers can auto-detect USB connected devices.
222: 
223: Beyond strict serial communication over COM ports (discussed above), the
224: conn= property can also address specific USB devices, as well as specify TCP
225: or VXI communication parameters. See these examples:
226: 
227:  $ sigrok-cli --driver <somedriver>:conn=<vid>.<pid> ...
228:  $ sigrok-cli --driver <somedriver>:conn=tcp-raw/<ipaddr>/<port> ...
229:  $ sigrok-cli --driver <somedriver>:conn=vxi/<ipaddr> ...
230:  $ sigrok-cli --driver <somedriver>:conn=usbtmc/<bus>.<addr> ...
231: 
232: Individual device drivers _may_ implement additional semantics for the
233: conn= specification, which would not apply to other drivers, yet can be
234: rather useful for a given type of device.
235: 
236:  $ sigrok-cli --driver <somedriver>:conn=sn=<serno>
237: 
238: 
239: Specifying serial port parameters
240: ---------------------------------
241: 
242: Every serial device's driver has default serial port parameters like baud
243: rate, number of data bits, stop bits and handshake status. If a device requires
244: different parameters, pass them as option "serialcomm" with the driver name.
245: See libsigrok docs for the function serial_set_paramstr() for complete specs.
246: 
247: Example:
248: 
249:  $ sigrok-cli --driver <somedriver>:conn=<someconn>:serialcomm=9600/7n1/dtr=1
250: 
251: 
252: Permissions of serial port based devices
253: ----------------------------------------
254: 
255: When using devices supported by libsigrok that use serial port based cables
256: (real RS232 or USB-to-serial ones) to connect to a PC, you need to ensure
257: that the user running the libsigrok frontend has (read/write) permissions to
258: access the serial port device (e.g. /dev/ttyS0, /dev/ttyUSB0, and so on).
259: 
260: You can use 'chmod' to apply permissions as you see fit, and/or 'chown' to
261: change the owner of the serial port device to a certain user or group.
262: 
263: For USB-to-serial based devices, we recommended using our udev rules file
264: (see below for details).
265: 
266: 
267: Permissions for USB devices (udev rules files)
268: ----------------------------------------------
269: 
270: When using USB-based devices supported by libsigrok, the user running the
271: libsigrok frontend (e.g. sigrok-cli) has to have (read/write) permissions
272: for the respective USB device.
273: 
274: On Linux, this is accomplished using udev rules. libsigrok ships a rules
275: file containing all supported devices which can be detected reliably
276: (generic USB-to-serial converters are omitted, as these are used for a wide
277: range of devices, e.g. GPS receivers, which are not handled by libsigrok).
278: 
279: The file is available in contrib/60-libsigrok.rules. This file just contains
280: the list of devices and flags these devices with ID_SIGROK="1". Access is
281: granted by the 61-libsigrok-plugdev.rules or 61-libsigrok-uaccess.rules files,
282: allowing access to members of the plugdev group or to currently logged in
283: users, respectively.
284: 
285: When using a libsigrok package from your favorite Linux distribution, the
286: files should already be installed in /usr/lib/udev/rules.d/, i.e.
287: 60-libsigrok.rules and one of the access granting rules files. Use of
288: 61-libsigrok-uaccess.rules is encouraged on systemd distributions.
289: 
290: The access policy can be locally overridden by placing appropriate rules in
291: /etc/udev/rules.d/, disabling or amending the default policy. See the
292: udev documentation, e.g. man 7 udev, for details.
293: 
294: If you're building from source, you need to copy the file to the place
295: where udev will read these rules. Local rules should go to /etc/udev/rules.d.
296: Keep the file naming, otherwise interaction between the libsigrok rules and
297: rules shipped by the system will be broken.
298: 
299: Please consult the udev docs for details.
300: 
301: 
302: Assigning drivers to devices (Windows, Zadig)
303: ---------------------------------------------
304: 
305: On Windows systems it may be necessary to assign drivers to devices
306: before libusb based applications can access them. It may be necessary
307: to re-run this driver assignment after firmware upload in case the
308: device changes its USB identification as a consequence of loading the
309: firmware image.
310: 
311: The https://sigrok.org/wiki/Windows wiki page discusses this subject,
312: and other platform specific aspects.
313: 
314: 
315: Non-default drivers for commodity chips
316: ---------------------------------------
317: 
318: Some vendors include common USB chips in their products yet assign device
319: specific VID:PID pairs. Which results in the necessity for extra steps
320: before the serial port can be used:
321: 
322: - GW Instek VCP, found in GDM-8000 and probably other meters: Install the
323:   vendors Windows driver to get access to a COM port. Or force the driver
324:   assignment on Linux:
325:     # modprobe cp210x
326:     # echo 2184 0030 > /sys/bus/usb-serial/drivers/cp210x/new_id
327: 
328: 
329: Cypress FX2 based devices
330: -------------------------
331: 
332: Devices using the Cypress FX2(LP) chip without any specific USB VID/PID will
333: be enumerated with VID/PID 04b4:8613 (the default for "unconfigured FX2").
334: These are usually "FX2 eval boards" (that can also be used as LAs, though).
335: 
336: On Linux, the 'usbtest' driver will usually grab such devices, and they will
337: thus not be usable by libsigrok (and frontends).
338: 
339: You can fix this by running 'rmmod usbtest' as root before using the device.
340: 
341: 
342: UNI-T DMM (and rebranded models) cables
343: ---------------------------------------
344: 
345: UNI-T multimeters (and rebranded devices, e.g. some Voltcraft models) can
346: ship with different PC connectivity cables:
347: 
348:  - UT-D02 (RS232 cable)
349:  - UT-D04 (USB/HID cable with Hoitek HE2325U chip, USB VID/PID 04fa:2490)
350:  - UT-D04 (USB/HID cable with WCH CH9325 chip, USB VID/PID 1a86:e008)
351:  - UT-D07 (Bluetooth adapter, ISSC BL79 BLETR chip)
352:  - UT-D09 (USB/HID cable with SiL CP2110 chip, USB VID/PID 10c4:ea80)
353: 
354: The above cables are all physically compatible (same IR connector shape)
355: with all/most currently known UNI-T multimeters. For example, you can
356: use either of the UT-D04 USB/HID cables or the UT-D02 RS232 cable with
357: the UNI-T UT61D multimeter.
358: 
359: When using the UT-D02 RS232 cable with any of the supported UNI-T DMMs,
360: you have to use the respective driver with a '-ser' drivername suffix
361: (internally all of these models are handled by the 'serial-dmm' driver).
362: 
363: You also need to specify the serial port via the 'conn' option, e.g.
364: /dev/ttyUSB0 (attached via a USB-to-serial cable) or /dev/ttyS0 (actual
365: RS232 port) on Linux (see above).
366: 
367: Finally, the user running the frontend (e.g. sigrok-cli) also needs
368: permissions to access the respective serial port (see above).
369: 
370: Examples (sigrok-cli):
371: 
372:  $ sigrok-cli --driver uni-t-ut61e-ser:conn=/dev/ttyUSB0 ...
373:  $ sigrok-cli --driver voltcraft-vc820-ser:conn=/dev/ttyS0 ...
374:  $ sigrok-cli --driver uni-t-ut61e-ser:conn=hid/cp2110
375: 
376: Using any of the UT-D04 et al USB/HID cables can be done in two different
377: ways: Use transparent serial over HID support in libsigrok, by giving the
378: -ser driver a conn=hid/... serial port spec. This re-uses the 'serial-dmm'
379: driver, results in better coverage of these code paths, and reduces
380: maintenance overhead. Or by running non-ser drivers and passing USB
381: specific connection details. When the driver _without_ the '-ser' suffix
382: is used, the models are handled by the 'uni-t-dmm' driver. These duplicate
383: drivers only exist for historical reasons, the redundancy may result in
384: differences of behaviour between the two implementations. When in doubt,
385: check if the '-ser' driver works for you.
386: 
387: In the USB specific driver case you need to specify the cable's vendor
388: and product IDs. Autodetection is not possible here, since various other
389: products use the USB VID/PID of those cables too, and there is no way to
390: distinguish them. The sigrok software errs on the safe side, and won't
391: communicate to serial ports unless explicitly instructed by the user.
392: 
393: The user running the frontend does also need to have permissions to
394: access the respective USB device (see above).
395: 
396: Examples (sigrok-cli):
397: 
398:  $ sigrok-cli --driver uni-t-ut61e:conn=1a86.e008 ...
399:  $ sigrok-cli --driver voltcraft-vc820:conn=04fa.2490 ...
400: 
401: 
402: UNI-T UT-D04 cable issue on Linux
403: ---------------------------------
404: 
405: The UNI-T UT-D04 cable with Hoitek HE2325U (or WCH CH9325) chip seems to have
406: a very specific problem on Linux. Apparently it requires to be put into
407: suspend (and woken up again) before it is usable. This seems to be a
408: Linux-only issue, Windows is not affected by this since apparently the
409: Windows kernel does this for every USB device, always.
410: 
411: Thus, if you want to use any of the UNI-T DMMs with this specific cable,
412: you'll have to run the following script (as root) once, every time you attach
413: the cable via USB. The script was written by Ralf Burger.
414: 
415: See also: http://erste.de/UT61/index.html
416: 
417:   #!/bin/bash
418:   for dat in /sys/bus/usb/devices/*; do
419:     if test -e $dat/manufacturer; then
420:       grep "WCH.CN" $dat/manufacturer > /dev/null && echo auto > ${dat}/power/level && echo 0 > ${dat}/power/autosuspend
421:     fi
422:   done
423: 
424: 
425: UNI-T UT-D04 cable issue on Windows
426: -----------------------------------
427: 
428: There have been reports that CH9325 based cables are not detected on
429: Windows out of the box when they are assigned to libwdi drivers. Though
430: they may be usable in that case when the USB address is manually specified.
431: This can happen when some "USB to serial" driver is assigned which does not
432: provide a genuine COM port that enumerates naturally. Manually assigning a
433: "USB input device" driver can improve HIDAPI compatibility and make the
434: cable show up in sigrok's serial port enumeration.
435: 
436: 
437: Enabling multimeter / data logger measurement output
438: ----------------------------------------------------
439: 
440: Some multimeters or data loggers will not start outputting measurement data
441: unless a certain action has been performed by the user beforehand. This is
442: usually mentioned in the vendor manual of the respective device, but here's
443: a short list for convenience:
444: 
445:  - BBC Goertz Metrawatt M2110: Briefly press the "Start/Reset" button on the
446:    interface panel on top.
447:  - Brymen BM257s: Press HOLD during power-on.
448:  - Digitek DT4000ZC: Briefly press the "RS232" button.
449:  - EEVBlog 121GW: Hold "1ms PEAK" until the "BT" indicator is shown.
450:  - ES51919 based LCR meters (DER EE DE-5000, PeakTech 2170, UNI-T UT612):
451:    Press the button with the "RS232" or "USB" or "PC link" label (usually
452:    the "up" cursor button).
453:  - Gossen Metrawatt Metrahit 1x/2x devices, driver gmc-mh-1x-2x-rs232:
454:    - Power on the device with the "DATA" button pressed.
455:    - Metrahit 2x devices must be configured for the respective interface type.
456:  - Gossen Metrawatt Metrahit 2x devices, driver gmc-mh-2x-bd232:
457:    - 'BD232' interface:
458:       The multimeter must be configured for the respective interface type.
459:    - 'SI232-II' interface ("PC Mode"):
460:       The multimeter must be configured for interface type 'BD232' (all),
461:       'SI232 online' (28-29S) or 'SI232 store' (22-26x). The interface must
462:       be configured to the same baud rate as the host (default 9600).
463:       Multimeter and interface must be configured to the same address.
464:  - GW Instek GDM-397: Press the "REL/RS232C (USB)" button for roughly 1 second.
465:  - GW Instek VCP: See the discussion on manual driver assignment to common
466:    USB to UART chips with non-default USB identification.
467:  - MASTECH MS6514: Press the "Setup/PC-Link" button for roughly 3 seconds.
468:  - Meterman 38XR: Press the "RS232" button.
469:  - Metrix MX56C: Press the PRINT button to have the meter send acquisition
470:    data via IR. Hold the PRINT button to adjust the meter's transmission
471:    interval.
472:  - Norma DM950: If the interface doesn't work (e.g. USB-RS232 converter), power
473:    on the device with "FUNC" pressed (to power the interface from the DMM).
474:  - PCE PCE-DM32: Briefly press the "RS232" button.
475:  - RadioShack 22-812: Press and hold "SELECT" and "RANGE" together.
476:  - TekPower TP4000ZC: Briefly press the "RS232" button.
477:  - Tenma 72-7750: Briefly press the "RS232C" button.
478:  - UNI-T UT60G: Briefly press the "RS232C" button.
479:  - UNI-T UT61B/C/D: Press the "REL/RS232/USB" button for roughly 1 second.
480:  - UNI-T UT71x: Press the "SEND/-/MAXMIN" button for roughly 1 second.
481:    Briefly pressing the "EXIT" button leaves this mode again.
482:  - UNI-T UT181A: In the "SETUP" menu set "Communication" to "ON".
483:  - UNI-T UT325: Briefly press the "SEND" button (as per manual). However, it
484:    appears that in practice you don't have to press the button (at least on
485:    some versions of the device), simply connect the device via USB.
486:  - V&A VA18B/VA40B: Keep the "Hz/DUTY" key pressed while powering on the DMM.
487:  - Victor 70C/86C: Press the "REL/RS232" button for roughly 1 second.
488:  - Voltcraft VC-830: Press the "REL/PC" button for roughly 2 seconds.
489:  - Voltcraft VC-870: Press the "REL/PC" button for roughly 1 second.
490: 
491: 
492: ASIX OMEGA in RTM CLI mode
493: --------------------------
494: 
495: The asix-sigma driver can detect the Omega devices' presence, but does
496: not support their protocol and emits a diagnostics message. The firmware
497: image is not available for distribution, and information on the protocol
498: is not available. That's why native support is in some distant future.
499: Yet basic operation of Omega devices is available by using the vendor's
500: command line application for real time mode (RTM CLI).
501: 
502: The vendor application targets Windows (on x86), but also executes on
503: Linux when 32bit libraries for FTDI communication are provided. The
504: user manual discusses the installation. The sigrok asix-omega-rtm-cli
505: driver uses the vendor provided omegartmcli.exe binary to configure the
506: device for streaming, and to acquire sample data.
507: 
508: Either make an "omegartmcli" executable available in PATH. This can be
509: the vendor's executable or some wrapper around it or a symlink to it.
510: Or specify the executable's location in the OMEGARTMCLI environment
511: variable. The sigrok driver accepts an optional serial number (six or
512: eight hex digits) to select one out of several connected devices.
513: 
514:   (optional)
515:   $ export "OMEGARTMCLI=$HOME/.wine/drive_c/progx86/ASIX/SIGMA/omegartmcli.exe"
516: 
517:   (optional)
518:   $ OMEGASN=":conn=sn=a6030123"
519: 
520:   (example use)
521:   $ sigrok-cli -d asix-omega-rtm-cli${OMEGASN} --show
522:   $ sigrok-cli -d asix-omega-rtm-cli${OMEGASN} -o capture.sr --time 10s
523:   $ sigrok-cli -d asix-omega-rtm-cli${OMEGASN} -o capture.sr --samples 100m
524:   $ pulseview  -d asix-omega-rtm-cli${OMEGASN}
525: 
526: The RTM mode of operation samples 16 channels at a fixed rate of 200MHz.
527: Hardware triggers are not available in this mode. Glib should handle
528: platform specific details of external process execution, but the driver
529: was only tested on Linux so far. Acquisition start in sigrok applications
530: may take some time before sample data becomes available (roughly one
531: second here on a slow machine). This is an implementation detail of the
532: RTM CLI approach including execution under wine.
533: 
534: The reliability of that setup in the presence of fast changing input
535: signals is yet to get determined. It's assumed that slow input signals
536: are operational. It's essential that the _average_ rate of changes in
537: the input signal in combination with the hardware compression are such
538: that the FTDI FIFO can communicate all involved data via USB2.0 to the
539: application. Intermediate bursts of rapid changes shall not be an issue
540: given the Omega devices' deep memory which RTM uses for buffering.
541: 
542: Native support for the Asix Omega devices depends on the availability of
543: a protocol description and use of the protocol depends on the firmware's
544: availability at the user's site. Which then would allow to capture to
545: DRAM at high rates without the communication bottleneck, before the data
546: gets communicated to the PC after the acquisition has completed. Compare
547: the native sigrok support for Asix Sigma.
548: 
549: 
550: ChronoVu LA8/LA16 USB VID/PIDs
551: ------------------------------
552: 
553: The ChronoVu LA8/LA16 logic analyzer is available in two revisions. Previously,
554: the device shipped with a USB VID/PID of 0403:6001, which is the standard ID
555: for FTDI FT232 USB chips.
556: 
557: Since this made it hard to distinguish the LA8/LA16 from any other device
558: with this FTDI chip connected to the PC, the vendor later shipped the
559: device with a USB VID/PID of 0403:8867.
560: 
561: The 'chronovu-la' driver in libsigrok supports both VID/PID pairs and
562: automatically finds devices with either VID/PID pair.
563: 
564: 
565: OLS
566: ---
567: 
568: The Dangerous Prototypes Openbench Logic Sniffer (OLS) logic analyzer
569: driver in libsigrok assumes a somewhat recent firmware has been flashed onto
570: the OLS (it doesn't need a firmware upload every time it's attached via USB,
571: since the firmware is stored in the device permanently).
572: 
573: The most recent firmware version that is tested is 3.07.
574: 
575: If you use any older firmware and your OLS is not found or is not working
576: properly, please upgrade to at least this firmware version. Check the
577: Dangerous Prototypes wiki for firmware upgrade instructions:
578: 
579:  http://dangerousprototypes.com/docs/Logic_Sniffer_upgrade_procedure
580: 
581: Also, you need to specify a serial port for the OLS in the frontends, e.g.
582: using the 'conn' option in sigrok-cli, and you also need to have the
583: permissions to access the serial port (see above).
584: 
585: Example:
586: 
587:  $ sigrok-cli --driver ols:conn=/dev/ttyACM0 ...
588: 
589: 
590: JTAGulator
591: ----------
592: 
593: The Grand Idea Studio JTAGulator also implements the SUMP protocol and
594: thus is covered by the OLS driver. See the vendor's wiki on details how
595: to enable the Logic Analyzer mode of operation.
596: 
597:   https://github.com/grandideastudio/jtagulator/wiki/Logic-Analyzer
598: 
599: 
600: Mooshimeter
601: -----------
602: 
603: The Mooshim Engineering Mooshimeter is controlled via Bluetooth Low Energy
604: (sometimes called Bluetooth 4.0), as such it requires a supported Bluetooth
605: interface available. The 'conn' option is required and must contain the
606: Bluetooth MAC address of the meter.
607: 
608: Example:
609: 
610:   $ sigrok-cli --driver mooshimeter-dmm:conn=12-34-56-78-9A-BC ...
611: 
612: Since the Mooshimeter has no physical interface on the meter itself, the
613: channel configuration is set with the 'channel_config' option. The format
614: of this option is 'CH1,CH2' where each channel configuration has the form
615: 'MODE:RANGE:ANALYSIS', with later parts being optional. In addition for
616: CLI compatibility, the ',' in the channels can also be a '/' and the ':' in
617: the individual configuration can be a ';'.
618: 
619: Available channel 1 modes:
620: 
621:   - Current, A: Current in amps
622:   - Temperature, T, K: Internal meter temperature in Kelvin
623:   - Resistance, Ohm, W: Resistance in ohms
624:   - Diode, D: Diode voltage
625:   - Aux, LV: Auxiliary (W input) low voltage sensor (1.2V max)
626: 
627: Available channel 2 modes:
628: 
629:   - Voltage, V: Voltage
630:   - Temperature, T, K: Internal meter temperature in Kelvin
631:   - Resistance, Ohm, W: Resistance in ohms
632:   - Diode, D: Diode voltage
633:   - Aux, LV: Auxiliary (W input) low voltage sensor (1.2V max)
634: 
635: Only one channel can use the shared inputs at a time (e.g. if CH1 is measuring
636: resistance, CH2 cannot measure low voltage). Temperature is excepted from
637: this, so the meter can measure internal temperature and low voltage at the
638: same time.
639: 
640: Additionally, the meter can calculate the real power of both channels. This
641: generally only makes sense when CH1 is set to current and CH2 is set to a
642: voltage and so it is disabled by default. It must be enabled by enabling the
643: 'P' channel (the third channel).
644: 
645: The range of the channel specification sets the maximum input for that channel
646: and is rounded up to the next value the meter itself supports. For example,
647: specifying 50 for the voltage will result in the actual maximum of 60.
648: Specifying 61 would result in 600. If omitted, sigrok will perform
649: auto-ranging of the channel by selecting the next greater value than the
650: latest maximum.
651: 
652: The analysis option sets how the meter reports its internal sampling buffer
653: to sigrok:
654: 
655:  - Mean, DC: The default is a simple arithmetic mean of the sample buffer
656:  - RMS, AC: The root mean square of the sample buffer
657:  - Buf, Buffer, Samples: Report the entire sample buffer to sigrok. This
658:    results in packets that contain all the samples in the buffer instead
659:    of a single output value.
660: 
661: The size of the sample buffer is set with the 'avg_samples' option, while
662: the sampling rate is set with the 'samplerate' option. So the update rate
663: is avg_samples/samplerate. Both are rounded up to the next supported value
664: by the meter.
665: 
666: Example:
667: 
668:   $ sigrok-cli -c channel_config="Aux;0.1/T" --driver mooshimeter-dmm...
669:   $ sigrok-cli -c channel_config="A;;AC/V;;AC" --driver mooshimeter-dmm...
